newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst revises down EU grain sowings forecast.
newsitem.headline: Analyst revises down EU grain sowings forecast.

text.p: French grain analyst Strategie Grains said on Monday it had revised downwards its estimate for European Union grain sowings for the 1997 harvest to 38.1 million hectares.
This would represent a rise of three percent over 1996 sowings, it said.
Last month Strategie Grains said 1997 grain sowings would rise four percent to 38.2 million hectares.

Strategie Grains also predicted grain production within the European Union might rise by two percent to 207.4 million tonnes compared with 206.7 million tonnes predicted in January and a revised 204.1 million tonnes produced previously.
Strategie Grains warned that these estimates remained subject to revision.
Yields forecasts were based on a long-term trend and weather would determine how yields would turn out, it said.
The latest forecast assumed 1997/98 grain yields would drop two percent to 5.4 tonnes per hectare from 5.5 tonnes in 1996/97.
Strategie Grains put 1997/98 soft wheat output at 93.1 million tonnes against 92.8 million tonnes forecast in January and a revised 91 million tonnes in 1996/97.
This assumed wheat sowings would rise three percent to 14.2 million hectares in 1997 and yield remain steady at 6.6 tonnes per hectare.
The analyst now targets barley production at 52.4 million tonnes against 52.3 million last month and 52.5 million in 1996/97.
It put barley sowings up four percent at 11.9 million hectares and yield down four percent at 4.4 tonnes per hectare.
Strategie Grains expects the European Union to produce 36 million tonnes of maize in 1997/98 against 35.5 million forecast last month and a revised 34.3 million produced in 1996/97.
Maize sowings would rise six percent to 4.4 million hectares and yield decline one percent to 8.2 tonnes per hectare.
